1password-ssh-push: git push failing with 'Permission denied (publickey)' on this machine means the 1Password SSH agent isn't running (it holds the GitHub key, not a plain ~/.ssh file). Fix: ask the user to open/check 1Password, then retry. Do NOT run ssh-add — the user has explicitly ruled that out as the wrong path.
absolute-path-edit-wrong-worktree: When Editing/Reading a shared doc (ledger.yaml, INDEX.md, CONVENTIONS.md, etc.) by ABSOLUTE path while working in a worktree, double-check the path actually points into the current worktree, not the primary checkout — typing the primary checkout's path from muscle memory silently edits the wrong copy (main gets dirtied instead of the worktree branch) with no error. Prefer cwd-relative paths for files inside the worktree. Caught and fixed live during fps-hnp/PR #351 before it was committed.
aggregate-py-unpaired-seed-median: experiments/lib/aggregate.py:46 computes delta_<cohort>_median as median_over_seeds(candidate_ll) - median_over_seeds(R0_ll) — a DIFFERENCE OF MEDIANS. The seeds are paired (same data, same folds; only random_state differs), so the MEDIAN OF PAIRED DIFFERENCES is the better estimator. Measured on batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement: the two disagree by up to 0.0127 nats per fold and FLIP SIGN on fold 2 (paired +0.0036, published -0.0090), enough to change a per-fold sign-agreement count. Deliberately NOT fixed (fps-2kc closed 2026-08-31): fps-e6i showed the per-fold screen delta barely predicts the arbiter at all (r = -0.096 over all stations), so correcting how a near-uninformative number is aggregated buys little, and changing it would move published per-fold columns for every candidate already graded. If you are about to READ per-fold screen delta signs, or if fps-nas makes the screen matter again, compute the paired version yourself — see experiments/2026-08-31_tau_distance_of_logloss_gain/README.md 'Incidental finding' and run.py's per_fold_delta_ll(paired=...) for both conventions side by side.
backfill-perf-work-needs-synthetic-bench:
Backfill-perf issues (the fps-53j/fps-2us family: preload-once-slice-per-snapshot fixes) usually carry an acceptance criterion like 'before/after wall-clock captured for a multi-snapshot backfill', modeled on the real 492MB/2.2M-row fuel_signal.db used in the profiling experiment (experiments/2026-08-10_backfill_requery_profile/). That DB is gitignored and was NOT present in any worktree as of 2026-08-10 (checked whats-next-ecf413 and the primary checkout, both empty) — don't assume it's there; check with 'find . -iname "*.db"' first since a future session's machine state may differ.

If absent: write a throwaway synthetic-DB benchmark (open_db(':memory:'), seed a few dozen stations across several LGAs with distinct addresses — INSERT OR IGNORE on stations dedupes on address_normalized, so identical placeholder addresses across stations silently drop all but the first — and a few hundred days of history), time the old per-snapshot-loop shape against the new batched/streamed function on identical data, and assert row-for-row parity. The absolute speedup will be much smaller than the production-scale profiled number (small row counts don't stress the re-query cost the fix targets) — report it as a parity+directional-speedup check, and cite the experiment README's production-scale projection as the actual evidence for the acceptance criterion, not the synthetic number alone.
baseline-fingerprint-before-comparing-ru:
Before comparing the numbers from two experiment runs, compare their BASELINE FINGERPRINTS. Different fingerprint = not commensurable, whatever the deltas say.

The fingerprint is '<n>:<sha12>', a sha256 over the ORDERED baseline column list (fuel_signal.features.baseline_fingerprint). The current lock is 54:1a6ec2d84a69. It is recorded in:
  - experiment meta.json      -> meta["baseline"]  (stamped automatically by experiments.lib.io.write_meta)
  - batch freeze.json         -> "baseline_fingerprint"
  - run results.json / facts.json -> meta["baseline_fingerprint"] + "n_baseline_columns"
  - experiments/results.csv   -> "baseline_fingerprint" column (derived from that row's own `features` list)

A null/missing fingerprint means the run predates fps-zci (PR #312, 2026-08-19). Do NOT substitute today's constants for it — that asserts the run used today's baseline, which is exactly the claim that was false for every batch0 run. The absence IS the signal.

Why this exists: two contract defects (fps-sa1, wrong column SET: a 64-column R0 including the rejected Phase 4b brand troughs; fps-zci, wrong column ORDER: the right 54 sorted alphabetically, which fits a different LightGBM model because ties break on feature index) were compared head-to-head against a correct June run for two months. Neither left any trace in the artifacts that recorded the runs. The fingerprint is the detector; docs/CONVENTIONS.md § "The baseline feature set is declared, never discovered" is the full rule.
batch-dir-vs-candidates-dir: experiments/batches/<batch>/ (runner's frozen-artifact dir: freeze.json, noise_floor.json, meta['batch_dir']) and experiments/candidates/<batch>/ (candidate modules' dir: batch.json, redundancy.write_batch_record's output) are TWO DIFFERENT directories with confusingly similar names/roles. A dossier_tables.py call site that wants batch.json must use run_dir.parent (== candidates dir), never meta['batch_dir'] — passing the latter always misses the file and produces a plausible-but-false 'record was never written' reason. Bit fps-qbv's first PR (#341); caught by review before merge. See docs/routines/dossier.md and experiments/pipeline/redundancy.py's batch_dir_for().
batch-freeze-stale-features: batch_freeze.py's refresh_db() now hard-gates BOTH DB staleness and features.csv/.parquet staleness — after 'make update' it also runs 'make features' (uv run python -m fuel_signal.features), aborting with DbRefreshError if either step fails. Fixed fps-3vo (PR #307, merged 2026-08-18); the old gap (freeze could silently pin months-stale features right after a fresh DB pull) no longer exists. No manual 'run fuel_signal.features before freezing' workaround needed anymore.
bd-dolt-remote-add-auto-commits-config: bd dolt remote add/remove auto-commits .beads/config.yaml's sync.remote key to git immediately, verbatim — including any embedded credentials in the URL. Never pass a credential/token-embedded URL to 'bd dolt remote add' in a real checkout; if you need to test an authenticated URL, do it in a throwaway remote name and immediately 'bd dolt remote remove' it, then verify with 'git log -p -- .beads/config.yaml' that no secret landed in a commit before pushing anything. If one does land, it's usually still local-only (git status/log can confirm before any push) — git reset --hard to the last clean commit discards it safely as long as nothing was pushed.
bd-field-wipe-recovery: A 'bd update <id> --description ...' (or any --field) with a wrong/short value OVERWRITES silently — no confirmation, no diff. Never run a speculative bd update with its output redirected to /dev/null; you will not even see the success line. RECOVERY is exact, so do NOT retype the lost text from memory (that introduces transcription drift in precisely the long text you are trying to preserve). bd auto-commits every write to the embedded Dolt DB, one commit per bd command, message naming the issue. From the PRIMARY worktree: 'cd .beads/embeddeddolt/<dbname>' (e.g. fps — NOT .beads/embeddeddolt itself, which is not a dolt repo), 'dolt log --oneline -n 10' to find the commit BEFORE the bad auto-commit, then 'dolt sql -q "SELECT description FROM issues AS OF <full_commit_hash> WHERE id=<issue-id>" -r json'. Write it to a file, 'bd update --description "$(cat file)"', then re-query AS OF HEAD and assert byte equality against the file before 'bd dolt push'. Note 'bd sql' itself refuses here: 'not yet supported in embedded mode' — use the dolt binary directly. Comments are separate rows and survive a description wipe.
bd-handoff-goes-in-description: bd ready / bd list return TITLE ONLY — no description, no comments. So the ONLY channel that reliably reaches whoever picks up an issue is the description body, read via 'bd show <id>'. Consequences when filing work: (1) Put handoff pointers (reference prototypes, experiment dirs, prior profiling, 'read X before coding') at the TOP of --description, above the What/Why sections. (2) 'bd comment' is for post-hoc discussion, NOT for handoff — bd show does render comments, but below the acceptance criteria, where a reader who thinks they've finished the spec has already stopped. (3) bd comments are APPEND-ONLY — there is no edit or delete (bd comments has only 'add'). A wrong comment can only be corrected by appending another one, which leaves the wrong text visible forever. This is a second, independent reason to put anything load-bearing in the description, which IS editable: 'bd update <id> --body-file <file>'. (4) bd hard-wraps long lines in show output and will break a long path mid-string (experiments/2026-08- / 10_backfill_requery_profile/) — put file paths on their own short indented line so they survive copy-paste. (5) The worker takes 'bd ready --label chore --unassigned --sort oldest -n 1', so a freshly-filed chore is picked up LAST, behind every older open chore — don't assume a new issue is next in line. Editing a description: 'bd show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].description'' (note: JSON is an ARRAY, .[0], not an object) to a file, edit, then 'bd update <id> --body-file <file>'.
bd-search-limits: bd search matches a CONTIGUOUS SUBSTRING OF THE TITLE ONLY, and hides closed issues by default. Both trip you up in the same way — a miss returns 'No issues found', which is indistinguishable from genuine absence. (1) Substring, not tokenized-AND: 'bd search "load once and slice"' matches the title 'Backfill range paths load once and slice', but 'bd search "load once slice"' finds NOTHING. Search one distinctive word ('backfill'), not a remembered phrase. (2) Descriptions are NOT searched by the positional query — use --desc-contains for that. So a decision buried in a description body is invisible to a plain title search; put the distinguishing words in the TITLE. (3) Closed issues are excluded by default but fully searchable with --status all. This does NOT justify leaving records open: when checking whether ground has been covered, the habit is 'bd search <word> --status all'. Corollary for AGENTS.md's decision-pointer convention: file the thin --type=decision record and CLOSE it immediately. An open issue means work outstanding; using open state to keep knowledge visible pollutes bd ready/bd list forever and misuses the work queue as a knowledge store. Durable instructions belong in channels that are PUSHED at session start — 'bd remember' (injected at bd prime) and AGENTS.md/CONVENTIONS.md (read at orientation) — not in ones that depend on someone running the right search.
beads-commit-tracked-state: Commit .beads/ changes with the work that caused them — do NOT gitignore interactions.jsonl. Under the Dolt backend the tracked git files are .beads/{.gitignore,README.md,config.yaml,metadata.json,interactions.jsonl}; everything runtime (embeddeddolt/, backup/, locks, *.db, sync state) is already excluded by .beads/.gitignore, which is bd's OWN maintained template — ~40 patterns long, and its closing comment states config files 'are tracked by git by default since no pattern above ignores them'. Omission from a list that thorough is a decision, not an oversight. interactions.jsonl is the append-only audit trail (kind:field_change, actor, old/new value, and the --reason text from bd close), so it carries the durable 'why' readable from a plain git clone WITHOUT a Dolt pull — bd history reads Dolt instead, so the JSONL is the git-side mirror and the only copy a fresh cloner sees. It is tiny (~5K). Leaving it dirty is the worst option: it accumulates silently and eventually gets swept into an unrelated commit. Commit it directly to main — it is tracked state, not code, and a PR over an append-only audit log is noise; the project's PR rule protects code. Note bd dolt push and the git commit are SEPARATE and neither implies the other: dolt push syncs the database, the git commit records the JSONL mirror. Do both. (Distinct from .beads/issues.jsonl, an export refreshed by the pre-commit hook only when export.auto=true — not enabled here.) Sources: beads docs reference/git-integration.md, core-concepts/sync-concepts.md.
beads-writes-through-to-primary-worktree:
This repo's .claude/worktrees/* are nested INSIDE the primary checkout (not sibling dirs), and only the primary worktree has ever had a live Dolt db (.dolt/, *.db — both gitignored, never initialized in the nested worktrees). So bd's db auto-discovery, run from ANY nested worktree, writes through to the PRIMARY worktree's .beads/interactions.jsonl, not the worktree you were actually in — confirmed empirically repeatedly (e.g. bd close for fps-2us on 2026-08-10 from worktree whats-next-ecf413 landed the field_change line in the PRIMARY's interactions.jsonl).

ACTION, not just awareness: during the post-merge checklist, a dirty .beads/interactions.jsonl in the PRIMARY worktree after bd work in ANY worktree is YOUR OWN pending write, not unrelated pre-existing state — commit it there and push (direct-to-main precedented, e.g. df61f89, 39eb6a4) BEFORE moving on. Do not report it to the user as a reason you skipped the ff-pull step; that under-delivers on a checklist item you have the information to finish. Sequence: (1) git -C <primary> status --short; if only interactions.jsonl is dirty, commit+push it there; (2) THEN re-check whether primary is behind origin/main and ff-pull if so (rebase the interactions.jsonl commit onto origin/main first if primary had already fallen behind — a plain push will be rejected non-fast-forward). Only treat the tree as genuinely blocking if something OTHER than interactions.jsonl is dirty (a real conflict/uncommitted work you can't attribute to this session's bd calls) — that's the actual 'don't risk it' case, not this one.
branch-before-first-commit: git checkout -b <branch> must be the FIRST git action in any implementation session, before any edit or DB-writing command. Committing to main directly has happened twice, each requiring a destructive git reset --hard + force-push to undo. If mid-session you realize you're on main: stop, branch, then continue — don't commit-then-fix.
branch-prs-from-origin-main: HARD RULE: always create PR branches with 'git fetch origin && git checkout -b <branch> origin/main', never off local main. This repo routinely leaves local main ahead of origin (experiment lab-book entries and results.csv lock rows commit direct to main, unpushed) — branching off local main bundles those unpushed commits into the PR's squash merge and diverges main from origin post-merge. Hit three times (PRs #256, #261, #304 — #304's unpushed commit was a docs fix, recovered with a verified-safe 'git reset --hard origin/main' since its content was already subsumed by the squash).
cadence-not-a-free-knob: Cadence is not a free knob in the backtest engine. run_backtest CLAMPS a dry tank to 0 and continues (its emergency rule tests the CURRENT level, not the post-depletion overshoot, despite its comment claiming otherwise), while run_oracle_backtest PRUNES run-dry paths. So oracle-vs-model headroom is only meaningful where no reachable level lands in the open (floor*size, D) interval, D = daily_consumption * evaluation_interval_days. Default TankParams: SAFE at 1, 2 and 7 days; INVALID at 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8-14 (at 3d that is 109 dry events / 389 L and headroom goes NEGATIVE, which is impossible for a true ceiling). Check the STARTING level (50% of tank) as well as the wait-chain rungs -- README.md:756's documented CLI example fails there and nowhere else. Before trusting any non-default cadence, audit it empirically (replay the engine's own level arithmetic over the fill ledger) rather than reasoning about the lattice. Fix + merge gate: bd fps-5mn.
candidate-output-align-by-index-label: Candidate-pipeline (fps-3jj) output must be aligned by INDEX LABEL, never positionally. differential_pit_test (experiments/lib/pit_test.py) compares by index label and its docstring explicitly permits a candidate's add_columns/add_axis to return rows in a different order (a df.sort_values() inside the candidate is blessed). So any consumer that does axis_series.to_numpy() / .values and zips it against frame's columns silently pairs each row with the WRONG station_code/date — validation passes, the run completes, and only the verdict is wrong. Use .reindex(frame.index) before .to_numpy(), or .loc[]. This shipped as a real bug in runner.py's _build_axis_lookup (found in the fps-hvi review of PR #299); note DataFrame['col'] = series is already label-aligned by pandas, which is why the two sites in the same function disagreed.
concurrent-worktree-commit-by-another-se: A git worktree directory under .claude/worktrees/ can be written to concurrently by another live session (the owner's terminal, or another Claude Code session) even while you are actively working in it — worktree exclusivity is per-branch-checkout, not per-directory-access. Observed live 2026-09-02 on fps-32h-fold-regeneration-eb7064: a commit (62cffe5, addressing a Sourcery review comment on PR #359) appeared in the local branch's reflog as a plain 'commit:' action mid-session, with no fetch/pull/merge on this session's part — discovered only by checking 'git reflog show <branch>' after a push showed an unexpected old-tip SHA. No conflict resulted (git commit/push are atomic), but don't assume a worktree's git state is exclusively yours: if a push's old-tip doesn't match what you last saw, check the reflog before assuming something is wrong.
decide-feature-parity-gap: fuel_signal/backtest.py's ModelStrategy.decide() (the realised backtest's live replay path) recomputes features from PriceHistory independently of fuel_signal/features.py's offline row-construction path (used by the WFCV screen). A new engineered-feature family (LGA/brand/network/TGP troughs etc.) landing in features.py does NOT automatically work in decide() -- it needs its own loop/cache wiring there too. This bit fps-3i7 (2026-08-18, PR #306): brand-trough columns worked fine offline for 3 months (commit 3f2dd29) but decide() only ever looped LGA_FEATURE_COUNCILS, so any feature_columns set including a brand-trough column (e.g. batch_freeze.py's resolve_baseline_columns()) aborted the realised backtest's baseline arm on the very first decide() call -- candidate-independent, since R0 carries no extra_feature_provider. When adding a new feature family, check decide() parity, not just features.py.
decision-flip-substrate-is-fills-not-row: rowpreds.parquet's proba is the wrong substrate for 'did the realised backtest's decision differ' — it comes from the WFCV screen's own multi-seed, uncalibrated fit_score (experiments/pipeline/runner.py's _run_wfcv_screen), a DIFFERENT model from the realised backtest's single-seed, OOF-calibrated, per-fold-tau-selected one (experiments/lib/realised.py's _train_calibrate_select_tau). Thresholding rowpreds' raw proba at a realised arm's own_tau compares a decision from one model against a tau chosen for another. fills.parquet is the tank simulator's own executed record and is the correct ground truth for 'did the two arms buy on the same days' — diff it directly (experiments/lib/flips.py, fps-gez) rather than re-deriving decisions from rowpreds.
default-flip-breaks-contrast-tests:
When you flip a DEFAULT, grep for tests that used the NEW value as their contrast — they silently stop asserting anything.

Found flipping TankParams.evaluation_interval_days 7 -> 1 (fps-oqz, PR #323). Six fps-15c tests proved "default and non-default are mechanically distinguishable" by comparing TankParams() against TankParams(evaluation_interval_days=1). After the flip both sides construct the SAME tank. Exactly one of the six failed loudly (an inequality assert); the other five kept passing while comparing a value to itself — a green suite that had quietly lost its guard.

The fix is to move the contrast arm to the OLD value (7d here), not to delete the test: coverage of an explicitly-passed non-default cadence is still worth having, and a test that just follows the default tests nothing about the default.

Same shape applies to any default: a sentinel, a feature flag, a model name, a path. The tell is a test whose two arms are "bare constructor" vs "constructor with X" where X is the value you are moving TO.

Related: baseline-fingerprint-before-comparing-runs (same family — two things that look comparable but aren't).
dolt-git-remote-push-needs-embedded-toke: bd's Dolt git-backed remotes shell out to the real git binary (not an internal HTTP client) — see dolthub.com/blog/2026-02-13-announcing-git-remote-support-in-dolt. Push fails with an interactive-credential-prompt error in non-interactive containers even when ambient git credential helpers make plain 'git push' work fine, because that ambient config isn't guaranteed to reach bd's invocation (known Dolt bug dolthub/dolt#10486, still open/unfixed as of 2026-08-14). DOLT_REMOTE_USER/DOLT_REMOTE_PASSWORD (from 'bd dolt push --help') do NOT fix this — those only apply to Dolt's separate Hosted Dolt SaaS remotes, confirmed by direct testing, not generic git-backed ones. The fix that works: embed a token directly in the remote URL (https://x-access-token:TOKEN@github.com/...), matching Dolt's own documented CI pattern. UPDATE 2026-08-14 (fps-sk0): this fix has a precondition that can silently fail — it needs 'gh auth token' (or equivalent) to actually resolve a REAL token, not a proxy placeholder. In one Claude Code Routines sandbox, 'gh' wasn't pre-installed AND could not be installed either (curl to api.github.com returned 403, downloading a GitHub release tarball returned 404 — that sandbox's egress only permits git-protocol requests and an internal MCP tool for GitHub access, no raw HTTPS to api.github.com or file downloads). In that case there is NO way to obtain a real token from inside the sandbox at all, and bd dolt push will always 403 until either Dolt fixes #10486 or the sandbox is provisioned a real static token. Don't assume installing gh is always sufficient — check whether the sandbox's egress even permits it first.
experiments-pipeline-import-cycle: experiments/pipeline module import cycle: dossier_tables -> runner -> batch_freeze is a load-bearing chain (runner.py imports from batch_freeze; dossier_tables imports from runner). noise_floor.py imports from BOTH batch_freeze and dossier_tables, so it must never be imported at module level by batch_freeze.py (would cycle: batch_freeze -> noise_floor -> batch_freeze) or by dossier_tables.py transitively. Same applies to dossier_tables symbols (e.g. NOISE_FLOOR_FILENAME) imported into batch_freeze.py — top-level import cycles back through runner. Fix used in fps-cf8: import inside the function body (deferred to call time), not at module top — by call time every module in the chain is already fully loaded, so the cycle never actually executes.
five-all-nan-lga-trough-columns:
Five LGA trough columns are 100% NaN in the real features frame: days_since_trough_entry_{bayside,botany_bay,hunters_hill,lane_cove,waverley}. They ARE in LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS (part of the 54) — their LGA never produced a confirmed trough event, so this is permanent structure, not a data bug to fix.

Consequence for anything that fits/regresses ACROSS the locked set at once: a complete-case mask (predictors.notna().all(axis=1)) selects ZERO rows and every result returns NaN, silently. This bit experiments/pipeline/redundancy.py's block-R2 check (fps-3jj.15): the screen printed a clean report and measured nothing. Fixed there by usable_predictors(), which drops all-NaN and constant predictors and discloses the drop in the report.

placebo.py meets the same five from the other direction (experiments/INDEX.md 2026-08-22: '5 all-NaN skipped, 49 usable' of 54).

Synthetic test frames will NOT reproduce this — smoke-run against data/features.parquet before opening the PR.
float-reformulation-not-strictly-more-ac: Float reformulations trade rounding-tie failure modes, they don't eliminate them: a/b < c and a < c*b round differently near boundaries, and size/(size/life) does not always recover 'life' exactly (double-rounding). A 'more exact' computation path (e.g. persisting raw fields instead of a display-rounded stamp) can be WRONG in cases where the old lossy path happened to round correctly by luck. Always sweep a wide config grid and check against exact rational arithmetic before claiming a reformulation 'removes' a tie or is 'mathematically equivalent' to what it replaces — verified in fps-o0h/PR #355 review (TankParams.full_to_empty_days: TankParams(50.0, 50.0/11) gives 10.999999999999998, not 11.0; level/size<floor vs level<floor*size disagree at size=50,daily=2.0,floor=0.14,level=7.0).
gh-pr-merge-worktree-conflict: gh pr merge --delete-branch fails with "fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree" whenever run from a git worktree (not the primary checkout) while another worktree has main checked out — gh's merge command tries to do local branch housekeeping (checkout base branch) that git worktrees disallow across trees. Fix: merge via the API directly instead, which never touches local git: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N>/merge -X PUT -f merge_method=squash. Skip the --delete-branch step entirely — this repo auto-deletes head branches on merge anyway (see github-auto-deletes-merged-branch), confirmed via git ls-remote after an API merge. Verify the merge landed with gh pr view <N> --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit.
gh-pr-view-json-fields: gh pr view <N> --json reviewThreads errors in this environment ('Unknown JSON field'). Use --json comments,reviews,mergeable,statusCheckRollup instead — reviews carries bot/human review bodies (inline comments embedded as markdown in the body), comments is PR-level top comments, there's no per-thread isResolved equivalent in this gh version.
git-pull-diverge-daily-snapshot: batch_freeze.py / make update's plain 'git pull' fails hard ('Diverging branches can't be fast-forwarded') if local main has ANY unpushed commit while the daily-snapshot GHA workflow pushes concurrently (pull.ff=only in this repo). Fix: git fetch + git rebase origin/main + push BEFORE running batch_freeze.py or anything that shells out to 'make update'. Don't leave commits unpushed across a work session in this repo.
github-auto-deletes-merged-branch: GitHub auto-deletes the remote branch on PR merge when the repo's 'Automatically delete head branches' setting is on (edwinsteele/fuel-price-signal has it on). After 'gh pr merge', don't assume 'git push origin --delete <branch>' is still needed — check first (e.g. 'git ls-remote --exit-code origin <branch>') or just let the delete fail harmlessly rather than treating it as an error.
github-issue-state-meaningless-post-migr: GitHub Issue open/closed state carries NO information about whether work is done in this repo. The Beads migration (2026-08-06) bulk-closed every GitHub Issue — gh #268, #271, #270, #32 and #6 all show closedAt within 22 seconds of each other at 2026-08-06T07:37. A bead's 'External: https://github.com/.../issues/N' link therefore points at an issue that is closed regardless of the bead's real status, and 'gh issue view N' will report CLOSED for live work. The bead is the only live record: check 'bd show <id>'. This misled a real session (2026-08-17: gh#268 read as closed while its bead was genuinely open with work outstanding). Corollary: never use gh issue state to reconcile bd state, in either direction. PRs are different — they still live on GitHub and their merged state IS authoritative.
graduating-a-column-is-two-edits:
Graduating a held-out feature column into the locked model contract is TWO edits, in the same change:
  1. add it to fuel_signal.features.LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS — APPEND, never insert or sort
  2. DELETE its entry from fuel_signal.features.NON_MODEL_COLUMNS

Do only step 1 and resolve_baseline_columns() raises NonModelColumnLeak; batch_freeze and the candidate runner abort. This is a hard stop, not a warning, on purpose: graduation is a declaration, not something the code should infer.

Why it works this way (fps-zci, PR #312): non_model_columns() decides a column's category from what the column IS — named in NON_MODEL_COLUMNS, or trough-prefixed and not one of the LGA troughs — and deliberately does NOT check whether the lock already claims it. A detector that skipped whatever the lock contains cannot detect a column wrongly IN the lock, which is the entire fps-sa1 failure (10 rejected brand-trough columns sitting in a 64-column R0 for two months).

Two traps at re-lock time:
  - ORDER is part of the contract. LightGBM breaks equal-gain split ties by feature index, so a permutation fits a different model (measured: 0.038 c/L on the pooled realised delta). Append leaves existing indices untouched; inserting or sorting does not.
  - tests/test_feature_contract.py asserts LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS == the artifact's feature_columns (ORDERED ==), but SKIPS when data/models/ is absent — and it always is in CI, since the dir is gitignored and ci.yml runs a bare `pytest -q`. Verify the re-lock LOCALLY; green CI does not mean the contract was checked.

Live case: tgp_delta_7d at the #271 chip-4 re-lock — bd fps-1785999729707-1-0301bf82, component 5 carries the full revised sequence.
handover-before-results-csv-write: When a rebuild reaches a step that writes to experiments/results.csv (score_phase2 without a skip flag, calibrate without --skip-results-csv, or any lock-row writer), stop and hand over to the user BEFORE running it. Don't run-then-revert — running the write is itself the violation, not just what's left afterward.
https-push-when-1password-agent-down:
When the 1Password SSH agent is down (git push -> 'Permission denied (publickey)'), you can still push and fetch over HTTPS without touching the user's remote config, because 'gh auth setup-git' has a credential helper installed: 'git push https://github.com/edwinsteele/fuel-price-signal.git <branch>:<branch>'. Use this when the owner is away and cannot open 1Password; still tell them SSH is broken.

GOTCHA THAT BITES NEXT: pushing via an explicit URL does NOT update refs/remotes/origin/main, and 'git fetch origin' fails for the same SSH reason — so origin/main silently goes stale. 'git worktree add -b <branch> origin/main' then branches from an OLD commit, which is how a fix worktree ended up missing an already-merged change (2026-08-19). Refresh the tracking ref the same way: 'git fetch https://github.com/edwinsteele/fuel-price-signal.git main:refs/remotes/origin/main'. Or just branch from local 'main', which stays correct. Do NOT run ssh-add — the owner has ruled that out.
icloud-conflict-copies:
OBSOLETE AS OF 2026-08-18 — kept only so a future session doesn't re-derive it. The repo MOVED to ~/Code/fuel-price-signal, which is NOT under ~/Documents, so iCloud Desktop & Documents sync no longer covers it. Verified 2026-08-19: repo realpath /Users/esteele/Code/fuel-price-signal, zero conflict copies anywhere in the tree. Do not go hunting for these; do not trust the old ~/Documents/Claude/fuel-price-signal path in any doc or memory (see reference_repo_path_migration).

IF the repo is ever moved back under an iCloud-synced dir, the detection recipe was:
  - conflict copies insert ' 2' (or ' 3', ...) BEFORE the extension: 'freeze 2.json', 'fuel_signal 2.db', even 'fuel_signal 2.db-wal' (the ' N' landing before the whole '.db-wal' is the giveaway — no process writes that name).
  - they are mode 0600 with ZERO xattrs; files our own code writes are 0644 with com.apple.provenance.
  - git status shows only a fraction: *.parquet, *.db and .venv/ are gitignored, so a 500MB 'fuel_signal 2.db' hides completely. Use find, not git status.
no-db-writes-before-pr-merged: Do not run any command that writes to fuel_signal.db until the PR introducing that code is merged to main. A SELECT-only query against the live DB is fine anytime, but a write using unreviewed code is the same class of mistake as pushing unreviewed code. For smoke-testing during development, use a temp/in-memory DB instead. Exception: user explicitly authorizes a live-DB write for a specific purpose.
noise-floor-fixture-needs-n-placebo-colu: A noise_floor.json test fixture for a candidate with 2+ columns MUST set n_placebo_columns explicitly, or dossier_tables._noise_band() defaults it to 1 (the pre-fps-3jj.14 assumption: a floor with no n_placebo_columns key predates arity-awareness and WAS arity 1) — a 2-column candidate against an implicit arity-1 floor silently triggers the ARITY refusal branch (available: false, reason_code floor_arity_below_run) instead of whatever the test actually meant to exercise. Bit tests/test_dossier_tables.py's new decision_flips tests (fps-gez, 2026-08-24) until n_placebo_columns was added to every noise_floor.json fixture using columns=[...] with 2+ entries.
noise-floor-force-vs-cadence-relock: noise_floor.py --force recovers a batch's floor after a COLUMN-LOCK graduation (fingerprint drift) but is refused by check_freeze_cadence after a CADENCE re-lock (e.g. fps-oqz 7d->1d) — the guard deliberately won't let freeze.json and noise_floor.json disagree on cadence. After a cadence re-lock, freeze a NEW batch instead of trying to recompute the old one in place (see docs/CONVENTIONS.md 'A re-lock invalidates the batch's noise floor'). This is what actually happened to batch0 on 2026-08-22 (fps-cds's original plan assumed --force would work and had to be superseded by fps-aay).
non-primary-worktree-branch-stale-after-:
When an interactive session in a per-issue worktree (not primary) branches OFF that worktree's own identity branch to open a PR (e.g. claude/<slug>), and later cuts a fresh PR branch from origin/main mid-session (per branch-prs-from-origin-main, because origin/main moved), merging that PR and deleting the temp branch leaves the worktree needing a manual step nothing in the standard checklist covers: it's now sitting either on nothing (branch deleted) or, if never switched, on its own identity branch several commits behind origin/main.

CLAUDE.md's post-merge checklist step 3 ("git pull --ff-only in any OTHER worktree... behind main and clean") is phrased for OTHER worktrees, not THIS worktree's own now-stale identity branch — easy to finish the checklist, report success, and leave the session on a phantom or stale branch.

ACTION after any PR merge from a per-issue worktree: run 'git branch --show-current'. If it's the temp PR branch (about to be deleted) or already behind origin/main, checkout the worktree's own identity branch and 'git pull --ff-only origin main' (safe when 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <identity-branch> origin/main' is true, i.e. nothing else advanced it independently). Verify with 'git rev-parse HEAD origin/main' matching. Do this proactively at the end of every PR-merge post-merge checklist in a non-primary worktree, not just when asked — the user had to ask for it explicitly in fps-3jj.13's PR #330 (2026-08-23) after noticing this exact gap.
np-std-float-degeneracy: np.std of identical floats is NOT 0.0 — guard band degeneracy with np.ptp, not `std > 0`. np.std([0.01]*20, ddof=1) == 1.78e-18 because 0.01 has no exact binary representation (0.02 -> 3.6e-18; 187.8 -> 2.9e-14; only exact 0.0 gives 0.0). A `band_std > 0` test therefore does NOT catch 'every draw landed on the same value' — the case noise_floor.py's docstring names — and a z of (delta-mean)/1.78e-18 is order 1e18. In dossier_tables._noise_band that read as a confident REJECT under the mechanical -t<z<t split and wrote 'rejected' into ledger.yaml: a wrong grade, not a refusal. Pair the check with float(np.ptp(deltas)) > 0, which is exact and zero iff the draws really are identical. Fixed on the sibling-bank path in PR #345, then on the canonical path in PR #346 (fps-tnz) — both now call a single shared _band_std_usable(deltas, band_std) helper (extracted after PR #346 review) so the two checks cannot drift apart again the way they did between #345 and #346. The same std==0-without-ptp-pairing pattern recurs uncorrected elsewhere in the repo (fuel_signal/shap_report.py, rank_partners.py, lga_shap_plots.py, dependence_grid.py) — tracked separately as fps-9rw.
pandas-assert-equal-default-tolerance-hi: pandas assert_frame_equal/assert_series_equal default to tolerance-based comparison (rtol=1e-5), which silently PASSES a real leak in a differential PIT/leak-detection test when values are large-magnitude — e.g. a whole-series mean of YYYYMMDD-scale price_date differed by ~1.5 out of ~20260812, well inside the default relative tolerance despite being a genuine, detectable leak. Any equality check whose JOB is to catch a difference (leak tests, point-in-time recomputation checks, idempotency checks) must pass check_exact=True explicitly — the default is for numeric-tolerance comparisons like float arithmetic results, not equality-as-a-safety-property. Found and fixed in experiments/lib/pit_test.py's differential_pit_test (fps-3jj.2, PR #298) via the runner's own new tests, not a pre-existing test gap.
primary-worktree-stray-branch-postmerge:
A code-review agent (or any subagent) that checks out a PR branch inside the PRIMARY worktree to inspect a diff can leave it stranded off main — a local-only temp branch (e.g. 'pr-308-review-tmp'), possibly pointing at a stale commit if the PR got more pushes after the checkout, plus stray untracked pipeline-run artifacts (results.json/rowpreds.parquet/fills.parquet from an unrelated candidate run) left sitting in the tree. Neither git status nor 'bd dolt push' surfaces this — only 'git -C <primary> branch --show-current' does. This breaks the post-merge checklist's assumption that primary is on main: committing the .beads/interactions.jsonl audit trail (see beads-writes-through-to-primary-worktree) onto the wrong branch would strand it off main's history.
ACTION: before the post-merge checklist's interactions.jsonl commit, run 'git -C <primary> branch --show-current'; if it isn't main, 'git checkout main' there FIRST (safe — a plain branch switch doesn't touch untracked files, and won't conflict on interactions.jsonl since PR commits never touch .beads/), THEN proceed with ff-pull + commit + push as normal. Leave any stray untracked artifacts and the abandoned temp branch alone — report them, don't delete without asking; they may be someone else's in-progress work.
prose-justifications-fail-silently: The claims that survive review are the ones nothing executes: prose asserting WHY something is the way it is. A helper's justification for existing, the guarantee a documented escape hatch offers, the population a number describes, a test's discriminating power. Tests fail loudly and types fail loudly; a justification fails silently forever, and the author is the last person able to catch it because they have already convinced themselves. PR #361 hit this three times in one review (all found by the reviewer, none by CI): '_placeholders exists because order matters here' — describe_universe sorts before calling it; 'this test fails if anyone reintroduces the second mechanism' — it does not, that form decides identically; 'three of these cases fail' — five do. The CODE was right every time. How to apply: when writing a docstring sentence of the form 'X is this way BECAUSE Y', ask what would fail if Y were false — if the answer is nothing, either delete the sentence, or attach the command/measurement that establishes it so the next reader re-derives rather than trusts. Prefer removing the fragility to documenting it (the two-mechanism coverage gate was refactored to one mechanism rather than given a warning comment). See [[test-discrimination-claims-need-mutation]] for the test-specific case, which needs a mutation run and not just reasoning.
results-csv-main-only:
experiments/results.csv (the canonical lock-history ledger) is only ever modified on main, and even then only after explicit user confirmation before running the write step. Never stage/commit changes to it from a feature/experiment branch. Per-experiment-dir results.csv files (e.g. experiments/l1_per_row_lga/results.csv) are a separate, always-fine convention.

SCHEMA changes count too, and need the same confirmation — asking is not optional just because no result row is being added. Precedent (fps-zci, PR #312, 2026-08-19): adding the baseline_fingerprint column required migrating all 29 existing rows, because log_experiment hard-fails when the on-disk header does not match _CSV_HEADER exactly. The owner explicitly approved doing it on the branch; that approval was for that change, and does not generalise.

Two traps found doing it:
  - Three legacy rows carry UNQUOTED commas in `notes`, so csv.DictReader parses them into a None overflow key and backtest_phase2.patch_results_csv's DictReader->DictWriter round-trip raises "ValueError: dict contains fields not in fieldnames: None". Repaired in #312 (overflow fields rejoined with ',' and re-quoted) and guarded by tests, but expect ragged rows in any similarly hand-written ledger.
  - Line endings: csv.writer defaults to CRLF while git normalises with core.autocrlf=input, and read_text/write_text silently normalise. That combination rewrote all 30 lines as invisible churn. Now pinned by .gitattributes (eol=lf) plus lineterminator="\n" in both log_experiment and patch_results_csv. Verify file edits on read_bytes(), not splitlines() — splitlines() strips both terminators and cannot see the flip.
screen-and-arbiter-share-no-population: The WFCV log-loss screen and the realised arbiter share 0.71% of their evidence. The screen scores every station (batch1: 798,649 rows, 714 stations); the arbiter replays only PREFERRED_STATIONS (261/414/429/585/18517) = 5,693 of those rows. realised.py trains on the full frame (train_df = a.df.loc[p.train_index]) and only the REPLAY is restricted, so the models are identical — it is the scoring population that differs, by 141x. Consequence measured on batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement (fps-e6i): per-fold corr(arbiter delta_cpl_own, screen delta_ll) is -0.096 paired / -0.176 published-convention over all 714 stations, and +0.478 / +0.543 with the screen restricted to the arbiter's five; sign agreement 7/14 and 5/14 vs 10/14 and 11/14. Population is the ONLY change (same model, folds, seeds, statistic); bootstrapped gap +0.574, 95% CI [+0.101, +1.033], P(gap>0)=0.991. The five stations are NOT special — their per-row gain sits 0.33 SE from the network-wide figure — they are just small enough that the effect cannot clear its own fold-clustered 2*SE even on log-loss, which is much smoother than realised CPL. So: a network-wide screen delta is not a forecast of a five-station CPL delta, and per-fold sign disagreement between them is the expected result, not a signal about the feature. fps-4z6 tracks reporting the restricted screen alongside.
search-artifact-noun-before-filing: Before filing a bead about an incident you just hit, search bd for the ARTIFACT NOUN, not the symptom — and put that noun in the title of what you file. Four separate sessions filed four beads for one dossier_tables.py bug over three days (fps-jrl, fps-d4g, fps-cl7, fps-rlh, untangled 2026-09-02) because each described the same incident with a different verb: 'wipes', 'clobbers', 'regressing', 'wiped'. Verbs never collide across filers; the artifact does. 'bd search "facts.json" --status all' returns three of those four today. The fourth (fps-cl7) evaded it only because its own title led with the action ('dossier_tables regen clobbers recorded grading') and never named facts.json — which is why this rule has two halves and the write half is the one that makes the read half work. This compounds bd-search-limits: search is a contiguous title substring, so a differently-phrased duplicate is invisible, and 'No issues found' looks identical to genuine absence. Corollary for reviewers: when several beads DO turn out to be one incident, merge into the best-written root-cause bead and carry the others' acceptance criteria across verbatim rather than closing them as pure dupes — fps-d4g's mtime-tie trigger was a genuinely second defect in the same file, and per feedback_fix_every_half_of_a_compound_defect both halves belong in one PR.
squash-merge-breaks-branch-ancestry:
A per-issue worktree's own identity branch, used directly as the PR branch (no separate temp
branch), can NEVER 'git pull --ff-only' back to caught-up after its PR squash-merges — this is
the expected terminal state, not staleness/data loss. Squash-merge writes a NEW commit on main
with different parents/hash than the branch's own commits, so 'git merge-base --is-ancestor
<branch> origin/main' returns false even when every byte of the branch's diff landed. Checking
staleness by ancestry alone gives a false positive here.

Verify correctly with content, not ancestry: 'git diff HEAD origin/main -- <files the branch
touched>' — empty output (or a diff containing only unrelated concurrent commits' changes) means
the branch's own work is fully landed. Confirmed 2026-08-27 on fps-1l1 (PR #339, worktree
fps-1l1-00d35d): branch tip c4aae01 is not an ancestor of origin/main's a5216ca, but diffing the
two touched files showed zero delta from this branch's own content — the only diff present was
PR #338's unrelated concurrent change to the same doc file.

Don't 'fix' this by checking out main in the worktree — the branch is finished and disposable;
the standing rule (feedback_no_worktree_cleanup_question / bd primary-worktree-stray-branch-
postmerge) is to leave a finished per-issue worktree as-is for a later cleanup session, not
switch its checkout mid-report. This is a DIFFERENT case from
non-primary-worktree-branch-stale-after-pr-merge (that one covers a separate identity branch
left behind when a temp branch was cut mid-session and later deleted) — that memory's
'--ff-only' remedy assumes a branch that CAN fast-forward; this one structurally cannot, ever,
once its own PR squash-merges.
status-rejected-means-graded-not-failed: runner.py's STATUS_REJECTED constant (value 'rejected') is written to EVERY candidate that completes a full graded run in results.json/facts.json — win, loss, or in-between. It is NOT a verdict, just 'the pipeline finished grading, here are real numbers' vs disqualified/aborted. Don't read status=='rejected' in a dossier artifact as 'the pipeline rejected this candidate' — check effect_delta_cpl_held / noise_band_z / clears_family_wise_threshold for the actual outcome. Tracked for a rename to STATUS_GRADED in fps-0z5.
tau-is-calibrated-not-raw: tau=0.25 is a CALIBRATED threshold; rowpreds.parquet 'proba' is RAW LightGBM output (experiments.lib.fit.fit_score never calibrates). They are not the same scale — the equivalent RAW threshold measured across batch1's 14 folds is 0.1136-0.1590, roughly half of 0.25. Comparing |p_raw - 0.25| is a category error worth ~0.10 of probability, and it lands in the most gain-dense bin of the distance profile, so it manufactures false confirmations. To convert: experiments/batches/<batch>/r0_cache.joblib holds the arbiter's per-fold fitted isotonic calibrator (per_fold[f]['cal_pipe'].calibrator) and own_tau. Isotonic is monotone, so p_cal >= tau <=> p_raw >= tau_raw and the whole analysis can stay in raw space once tau_raw is located by inverting the map. The screen's R0/seed-42 raw probabilities are byte-for-byte the arbiter's cached baseline scores (verified 2.98e-08 = float32 eps, fps-e6i), so this conversion is exact, not an approximation. Worked example: experiments/2026-08-31_tau_distance_of_logloss_gain/run.py (tau_raw, iso_levels, one_step_band).
tau-selector-is-cadence-blind:
score_phase2's tau selector is CADENCE-BLIND — it prints "Chosen tau = 0.25" at any cadence, so a tau that did not move after a cadence re-lock is NOT evidence the cadence change worked.

threshold_sweep() (fuel_signal/score_phase2.py:117) maximises (tp*6.37 - fp*5.80 - fn*11.14)/n over OOF PREDICTION ROWS. It takes y_true/y_pred and three cost constants — no TankParams, no tank state, no fill schedule — and tau is picked at step 3, BEFORE the tank is constructed for the backtest (score_phase2.py:495). Changing evaluation_interval_days cannot move it.

This is a known, MEASURED gap, not an oversight. fps-929 swept tau against realised CPL under the tank: best-in-hindsight is 0.35 at 1d, worth 0.062 c/L off 422 changed decisions whose effects cancel (at 7d the same comparison moves 8 decisions). Many flips + tiny delta = a real measurement of no effect, so tau stays 0.25 by decision.

Why they diverge more at 1d: at 7d the tank FORCES 67.6% of fills so the model's opinion is overridden two-thirds of the time and tau barely matters; at 1d only 21.4% are forced.

Harmless BY MEASUREMENT, not by construction. If the tank changes again (size, consumption, floor), nothing re-checks this automatically — the selector still will not be looking. Documented in docs/STATUS.md's cadence note.
test-discrimination-claims-need-mutation: A claim about a TEST's discriminating power ('this test catches X', 'N cases fail if you break Y') can only be established by RUNNING the mutation — and running it is only half the step. You must also read the part of the output that ANSWERS the question, not the part that happens to be on screen. In PR #361 the same docstring carried a wrong discrimination claim twice: 'this test fails if anyone reintroduces the second mechanism' (it does not; the alternative form decides identically), then 'three of these cases fail' (five do). The second was written WHILE the correct '5 failed' summary was printed one line below a 'tail -4' that had truncated the FAILED list to three. The CODE was right both times; the prose about what the code proves was wrong both times. Three habits. (1) Never write a discrimination claim you have not just run the mutation for. (2) 'tail -n' is a lossy summary chosen BEFORE you know what the answer looks like, and a count is exactly what it truncates — for any question of the form 'how many', grep the summary line or the full match set, never a fixed tail. This generalises past pytest to ruff, grep and long pipeline output. (3) When the claim carries a NUMBER, embed the mutation command in the docstring so the next reader re-derives it — a number in prose has no way to fail when the parametrize list grows underneath it. See [[prose-justifications-fail-silently]] for the general case.
venv-corruption-concurrent-uv: ModuleNotFoundError for 'six' or 'py' mid-session (even though uv sync reports satisfied) means .venv is half-synced from two concurrent uv run invocations racing. Only reliable fix: rm -rf .venv && uv sync. Avoid running uv run commands concurrently against this project; run pipeline stages sequentially.
webfetch-403-data-nsw-gov-au: WebFetch tool returns HTTP 403 on data.nsw.gov.au (bot-detection), but Python's requests library (used by fuel_signal/history.py) gets a clean 200 on the same URL. For any ad-hoc scraping/checking of this dataset (e.g. resource discovery, checking published month coverage), use requests/history.py's discover_price_resources() via Bash, or the in-app Browser tool — not WebFetch.
worktree-missing-gitignored-batch-data: Batch/candidate pipeline artifacts (data/features.parquet, fuel_signal.db, and per-batch/per-candidate features.parquet, fuel_signal.db, r0_cache.joblib, fills.parquet, rowpreds.parquet under experiments/batches/<batch>/ and experiments/candidates/<batch>/<candidate>/) are gitignored and do NOT exist in a fresh worktree checkout. Before running experiments.pipeline.shock_folds, dossier_tables, or any script that reads them, copy them from wherever they exist (e.g. the primary checkout) into the worktree first, or the run fails with FileNotFoundError. Confirmed live during the fps-hnp backfill (PR #351).
